result_semantic_payload.summary: Three of the four CRM orders are confirmed by the payment processor's settlement log: ORD-70231 (20000), ORD-70232 (15000) and ORD-70233 (31500). The linkage is a verbatim string match on the order id field — the settlement log's `order=` token equals the CRM `order_id` column value — corroborated by an exact agreement of the settlement `amount=` against the CRM `amount_usdt` for each matched pair. One settlement entry, `2024-06-02 settle order=ORD-72033 wallet=TXjkl444 amount=9999 ok`, must stay separate from the CRM orders: no CRM order has the id ORD-72033, and the README's stated rule is that a settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order. ORD-72033 is only a digit-transposition near-miss of the CRM's ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled), whose amount (9999 vs 8000) also disagrees, so no fuzzy or amount-based match is admissible. Separately, CRM order ORD-70234 has no settlement entry at all and therefore remains unconfirmed rather than mismatched.

claim_candidates.text: The CRM order table contains exactly four orders: ORD-70231 (wangqiang, 20000, paid), ORD-70232 (zhaolei, 15000, paid), ORD-70233 (sunli, 31500, paid) and ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled).

The payment processor's settlement log contains exactly four settlement entries: 2024-06-01 ORD-70231/TXabc111/20000 ok, 2024-06-01 ORD-70232/TXdef222/15000 ok, 2024-06-02 ORD-70233/TXghi333/31500 ok, 2024-06-02 ORD-72033/TXjkl444/9999 ok.
The README states that settlements reference CRM order ids verbatim, and that a settlement whose order id does not exist in the CRM table cannot be treated as the same order.

CRM orders ORD-70231, ORD-70232 and ORD-70233 are confirmed by the settlement log via a verbatim order-id string match, with the settlement amount equal to the CRM amount_usdt in all three cases (20000=20000, 15000=15000, 31500=31500).

The linkage field binding the settlement log to the CRM orders is the order identifier: the settlement log's `order=` token matches the CRM `order_id` column verbatim; the amount is a corroborating check, not the primary key.

The settlement entry for ORD-72033 (2024-06-02, wallet TXjkl444, amount 9999) must remain separate from the CRM orders because no CRM order carries the id ORD-72033, and the README's rule forbids treating such a settlement as the same order.

ORD-72033 should not be reconciled to CRM order ORD-70234 despite the visual similarity: the ids are a digit transposition, and the amounts disagree (9999 vs 8000), so no fuzzy or amount-based match is admissible.
CRM order ORD-70234 (qianer, 8000, cancelled) has no corresponding settlement entry, so it is unconfirmed rather than contradicted by the settlement log.

Coverage is 3 of 4 CRM orders confirmed (75%) and 3 of 4 settlement entries reconcilable to a CRM order (75%); the two unmatched items are asymmetric — one orphan settlement and one un-settled CRM order.

limitations: The task metadata reports no platform scenario and no registered source scopes; the delegated 'windows' scope is not reflected in the evidence inventory, which contains only three plain files rather than Windows registry/event-log artifacts.

All three files share a single creation timestamp (1790594136) and a single timeline cluster, so no independent chronology is available to validate the 2024-06-01/2024-06-02 dates recorded inside the settlement log.
No md5 hashes are populated for any file, so file integrity cannot be independently verified.
No file->cluster association facade is available (find_related_evidence returned no related items), so cross-file linkage rests on content inspection rather than server-side relations.

The reconciliation is limited to the fields present in the two files; there is no processor-side raw transaction feed, no CRM audit trail, and no evidence of whether ORD-72033 or ORD-70234 were later corrected.
Amounts are compared as recorded integers with no currency-normalisation or fee/tax adjustment, since neither file documents a fee structure.
warnings: Do not link settlement entry ORD-72033 to CRM order ORD-70234 on the basis of visual similarity of the ids; the amounts also disagree (9999 vs 8000).
The settlement log's `ok` status flag is not itself proof of CRM existence — confirmation requires the order id to resolve in the CRM table per the README rule.
